reasons: Only 8 of 17 sections were reviewed here, so the rest of the file is not described.
Zero inputs can cause divide-by-zero errors.
Facts and percentages are typed directly into the text.

terms.meaning: Inverter load ratio: the amount of solar panel capacity compared with the inverter's capacity.
Kilowatts of direct current capacity, the rated size of the solar panels.
Kilowatts of alternating current capacity, the output size the grid sees after the inverter.
Energy storage system, here a battery paired with the solar plant.
Investment tax credit, a government incentive that lowers the cost of a project.
The price measure the model reports per kWdc. Its full name is not stated in the code.
A Python text template that fills in values from the code while it runs.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the lecture agent
sections.what: Opens the file with a short description and brings in the data shapes the lecture fills in, along with typing helpers.
sections.why: Likely reason: the lecture is built from these shapes, so the output matches what the frontend expects.

sections.name: LectureAgent (part 1)
sections.title: Class setup and fixed lesson list
sections.what: Creates the lecture agent and loads a fixed list of lesson steps. Each step has a number, a title, the cost part it covers, and a picture name for the screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping the step order and wording as data makes every lecture consistent.
sections.watch_out: The component names here must match the names the step builder uses, or that step will come out empty.

sections.name: LectureAgent (part 2)
sections.title: Building the lecture steps
sections.what: Finishes the fixed list of steps for operations, the total, and the rest. Then it goes through each step, skips the storage step when storage is turned off, and creates the text for each remaining step.
sections.why: Likely reason: the storage step is optional, so skipping it avoids a lesson about a battery the project does not have.
sections.watch_out: Step numbers come from the fixed list, so skipping storage leaves a jump, such as step 3 followed by step 5.

sections.name: LectureAgent (part 3)
sections.title: Returning the finished lecture
sections.what: Returns the lecture package with the total step count, starting at step one with 0 percent complete. It also sends each step to its own builder by component name, and an unknown name produces an empty step.
sections.why: Likely reason: one routing point keeps each step's text in its own function.
sections.watch_out: A component name with no matching branch produces a blank lesson step without an error.

sections.name: LectureAgent: _generate_system_step
sections.title: System step and start of module step
sections.what: Writes the first lesson: the system size in megawatts, the DC to AC ratio, whether storage is included, and the matching AC capacity. It also starts the module lesson by working out the module area from the size and efficiency.
sections.why: Likely reason: the opening lesson gives the project's scale before the cost parts are explained.
sections.watch_out: A zero inverter load ratio or zero module efficiency would divide by zero and stop the lesson from building.

sections.name: LectureAgent (part 5)
sections.title: Rest of module step and start of inverter step
sections.what: Finishes the module lesson with the cost per kilowatt from the outputs, a worked cost example with a fixed 65, 25, and 10 percent split, and fixed text about module prices and market share. It also attaches the module research. Then it starts the inverter lesson, which explains the ratio and the extra DC share.
sections.why: Likely reason: the fixed split and facts make the lesson easy to read. The source for those facts is not shown.
sections.watch_out: Market facts and percentages are typed into the text, so they will not update when inputs or prices change.

sections.name: LectureAgent (part 6)
sections.title: Rest of inverter step and start of storage step
sections.what: Finishes the inverter lesson with the inverter type, its efficiency, the AC capacity, a worked cost example with an equipment and installation split, and a note on central versus string inverters. Then starts the storage lesson with the total battery energy in megawatt-hours.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: If the outputs do not include the storage result, its cost shows as zero without an error.

sections.name: LectureAgent (part 7)
sections.title: Rest of storage step
sections.what: Finishes the storage lesson with a short list of why storage matters, the efficiency and cycle life from the inputs, a worked cost example built from capacity, fixed project costs, and the tax credit, plus a cost split. It also attaches the storage research.
sections.why: Likely reason: the list and facts give context on why storage is part of the model.
sections.watch_out: The text states a 30 percent tax credit as fixed fact, but the amount used in the math comes from the storage input, so the two can disagree.

sections.name: LectureAgent: _generate_sbos_step
sections.title: Racking structure explanation step
sections.what: Builds the lesson step on the racking, the frames that hold the solar modules. It shows the racking area from the area-per-kW input and the system size, plus the cost per kWdc from the structural cost output. The wording changes depending on whether single-axis trackers are turned on. Part of the fixed-tilt wording was cut off in the packet, so it could not be fully checked.
sections.why: Likely reason: the lesson shows how the racking number was reached, using wording that matches the chosen design. Reason for the fixed cost split is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The cost split (50%, 35%, 15%) and the tracker energy gain text are typed in, so they do not update if the calculation changes, and the `web_research` parameter is accepted but never used.

sections.name: LectureAgent: _generate_ebos_step
sections.title: Electrical equipment cost step
sections.what: Builds the lesson step on the parts that collect and move power, such as transformers, breakers, combiner boxes, and wiring. It shows the AC capacity used for sizing, the shipping and tariff percentages from the inputs, and the electrical cost per kWdc from the output.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the user where each electrical cost comes from and how shipping and import tariffs add to it. Reason for the fixed component shares is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The component shares (25%, 15%, and so on) and the tariff range in the wording are typed in, so they can disagree with the model's own numbers when inputs change.

sections.name: LectureAgent: _generate_fieldwork_step
sections.title: On-site labor cost step
sections.what: Builds the field labor step: total hours (hours per kWdc times size), effective hourly rate with burden, and per kWdc cost taken from the computed fieldwork output MSP range. Fixed text gives a 60/30/10 split and regional wages.
sections.why: Shows how hours and burdened wage rates combine into labor cost.
sections.watch_out: Per kWdc figure comes from outputs, not computed here. Split percentages apply to the MSP minimum only. The 2,080 hours per person-year and wage ranges are hardcoded.

sections.name: LectureAgent: _generate_officework_step
sections.title: Office and soft cost step
sections.what: Builds the lesson step on office-based work: engineering, permits, project management, and legal. It shows office hours, the hourly rate with benefits, and the office cost per kWdc. It also gives typical permit and interconnection timelines as fixed text.
sections.why: Likely reason: explains that soft costs are office work rather than site work. Reason for the fixed split of office work is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Permit timelines, interconnection cost ranges, and the claim that soft costs are typically 50 to 100% of field labor are fixed text and may not match the user's numbers.

sections.name: LectureAgent (part 12)
sections.title: Taxes, contingency, and profit step
sections.what: Builds the lesson step on the final add-ons: sales tax, contingency, management overhead, and developer profit. It shows each rate as a percentage, the subtotal the rates apply to, and each add-on's cost per kWdc. The wording also labels the profit margin as competitive or high.
sections.why: Likely reason: each add-on is shown separately so the user can see how much each one adds. Reason for the 15% cutoff between competitive and high is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: If the total rate is zero, every add-on shows zero, which hides the problem instead of flagging it.

sections.name: LectureAgent (part 13)
sections.title: Add-on summary and running costs start
sections.what: Finishes the add-on step with its total and percentage split. Then starts the running-cost step, which describes yearly costs over the 20-year life of the plant, such as cleaning, inspections, inverter replacements, insurance, property tax, and land lease. It also adds up the fixed yearly costs for the summary.
sections.why: Likely reason: running costs are shown yearly, then as a present-value total, so the user can compare them with the one-time build costs. Reason for the fixed degradation and inverter replacement figures is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The running-cost text states fixed rates for inverter replacement and panel degradation as facts, so they will not change with the user's inputs.

sections.name: LectureAgent (part 14)
sections.title: Running-cost totals and summary start
sections.what: Finishes the running-cost step by giving the yearly cost range and the 20-year present-value range for the plant's size. Then starts the final summary step by collecting each component's result, the PV-only total, and, when storage is on, the PV plus storage total.
sections.why: Likely reason: turns per-kW figures into whole-project dollar totals the user can picture. The storage-only branch follows the storage setting in the code.
sections.watch_out: The upper annual cost figure uses a fixed capital cost of 100 million dollars instead of this plant's own cost, so it is wrong for any other project size.

sections.name: LectureAgent: calc_pct
sections.title: Final summary text and shares
sections.what: Builds the closing summary text: each component's median cost per kWdc and its share of the total, the PV-only total range, and the PV plus storage total when storage is on. It also writes project dollar totals and compares the median to a benchmark range.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The line saying every component is validated is fixed text, and this code runs no such check.
sections.watch_out: The benchmark line labels a per-kilowatt figure as per-watt, so the unit shown to the user is wrong even when the comparison itself is right.

sections.name: LectureAgent: get_step
sections.title: Step lookup and progress tracking
sections.what: Finds one lesson step by its number so the app can show it, and records which step the user is on with a completion percentage. Completion is the current step divided by the total number of steps, times 100.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app walks the user through steps in order and needs to know where they are. Reason beyond that is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A sequence with zero steps makes progress updates fail with a divide-by-zero error, and an unknown step number returns nothing with no message.

summary: Turns the cost model's inputs and results into a fixed, ordered set of plain-English lesson steps, each with an explanation, formulas, and a worked example.
purpose: Creates the step-by-step lecture that teaches a new user how each cost part was reached.
why: Likely reason: a lesson that explains each step helps a new user read the cost model. The class description calls the agent AI-powered, but the text in the sections shown is fixed wording with numbers filled in, and no AI call appears in them.
how: 1. Load the fixed list of 11 lesson steps, where the storage step is optional. 2. For each step, choose its builder by component name. 3. Each builder reads the inputs and outputs, works out a few numbers, and fills in the text. 4. Return the list with its step count and a starting position of step one at 0 percent complete.
inputs: The user's model inputs (CostModelInputs), the calculated outputs as a table of named values, and optional web research results for each component.
outputs: A LectureSequence: the total step count, and for each step a title, explanation, formula text, worked example, context, sub-parts, and optional research.
risks: Some builders divide by input values, so a zero ratio or zero efficiency would stop the lesson from building. Facts and percentages are typed into the text and will not update. Step numbers jump when storage is off. A missing output silently shows as zero. Only 8 of the file's 17 sections were included in this review, so the remaining sections are not described here.
debug: Check the step title and component name first. For a cost that shows as zero, check that the output key names match. For a crash, look for a zero input used in a division. A numbering gap when storage is off is expected.
